claims.text: Applying an aluminum oxide coating improves the high-temperature oxygen resistance of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed starting material is an as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is application of an aluminum oxide coating.
The coating produces an aluminum oxide layer that acts as the structural mediator.
The aluminum oxide layer forms a protective scale.
The protective aluminum oxide scale prevents oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
At 1000°C in air for 100 hours, the coated alloy will exhibit at least a 50% lower oxidation rate than the untreated alloy.
The proposed effect should apply from 900°C to 1100°C in oxidizing environments.
The coating's effectiveness in reducing atmospheres is uncertain.
A comparison of coated and uncoated samples at 1000°C in air for 100 hours can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the coated sample to show a statistically significant reduction in oxidation rate would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 50% oxidation-rate reduction, but the falsification rule only rejects the hypothesis when there is no statistically significant reduction. A significant reduction below 50% would fail the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
